identification: Collection of thimbles in a clear plastic stacking carousel. Photo 1 shows one tier plus the lid compartments holding about 26 thimbles; photo 3 shows the full carousel (several tiers, some thimbles visible below the top tray, including a blue stone-top thimble in the lid and a dark/brown one), so the total may be around 26-35. Mostly English hallmarked silver thimbles, c.1890-1930s (knurled tops, engraved star/daisy/diaper bands, one with a beaded rim), typical Birmingham/Chester makers (Henry Griffith, Charles Horner etc). One bright, deeply embossed one and some others may be base metal or plated (catalogue says 'predominantly' sterling). Current bid A$90, estimate A$150-250.

viewing_check: Count the thimbles in every tier, and how many are hallmarked. Look for stone tops (one blue visible), enamel, gold, named makers (Horner, Griffith, Fenton, Iles), souvenir or Australian-made ones, and any in cases. Note dents and holes in the tops. Weigh the silver ones if allowed.
